browser_ocr_surface_label: Example browser-integrated OCR and image-text-extraction posture for official voter-information routes
delivery_role_note: The service reviews official voter-information pages, images, and scans so browser-integrated OCR or image-text extraction remains subordinate to the original official artifact plus any reviewed text/help lane rather than quietly becoming a shadow official transcript.
downstream_transform_boundary_note: OCR-derived text is not silently promoted into an official translation, summary, or complete answer merely because later browser features can act on it.
extraction_boundary_note: Browser-generated OCR or image-text extraction remains subordinate to the original artifact and the current official help lane.
high_risk_topic_routing_note: When extracted text ambiguity affects deadline, location, eligibility, ID, cure, or rights-sensitive questions, the route moves the voter back to the current official help lane instead of pretending OCR settled the matter.
layout_dependency_note: If table structure, visual grouping, or nearby warnings matter, the route does not treat extracted plain text as a complete official answer.
official_text_equivalent_note: When decisive information exists in an image or scan, the office keeps an authored text/help lane available or makes clear that the extracted text is not a reviewed equivalent text edition.
original_artifact_recovery_note: The page preserves enough source-artifact identity and help routing that the voter can recover the original scan/image or the current official text/help lane without guesswork.
privacy_minimization_note: The service preserves route IDs, artifact IDs, reviewed extraction-context labels, policy notes, and timestamps rather than individualized OCR transcripts or clipboard histories.

reviewed_extraction_contexts.context_note: Reviewed likely OCR/search/copy behavior for scanned PDFs opened in supported viewers.
Reviewed likely copy/select/action behavior for image-based official notices or infographics.
Reviewed whether extracted text could be wrongly treated as a complete answer once translated, summarized, or copied elsewhere.
